title: The kingfisher's blue isn't pigment

scenes.headline: There's no blue paint in these feathers.
The blue is built, not dyed
scenes.body: Tiny sponge-like structures inside the feather barbs scatter blue light.
scenes.source: Stavenga et al. 2011, J. Exp. Biol.

scenes.headline: The orange is real pigment
scenes.body: Breast feathers hold pigment granules, so one bird makes colour two different ways.

scenes.headline: Why the back shimmers as it turns
scenes.body: Structural colour shifts with viewing angle. Pigment colour scatters evenly.

caption:
Kingfisher blue is made by structure, not pigment.

The cyan back and blue tail feathers use slightly different sponge structures, which is why they are two different shades of blue.

Source: Stavenga, Tinbergen, Leertouwer & Wilts 2011, Journal of Experimental Biology. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Fact-over-footage on a species common at Bengaluru lakes; the overlay explains physics the viewer can't see, which is what makes CC footage original.
